summary: `flume status`'s unstattable stop-flag refusal names the resolved path, not the bare artifact name
acceptance: the EX_IOERR stop-flag refusal in `status` states `stop flag at <path>`; a `flume status` run over a self-referential `.flume/stop` prints that phrasing, and the arm's path assertion no longer depends on the errno text
tests: `flume status`'s unstattable stop-flag refusal names the resolved stop-flag path, not the bare artifact name
notes: Line 380 is the last path-in-hand `status:` refusal printing STATE_ROOT_NAMES alone; lines 352 and 418 name paths, item 3 of the cite owes the path for this artifact, and `loop`'s own arm (1149) spells it. `statusStopPath` is already plain — no `plainPath` fold, matching the siblings. tick-verdicts.jsonl arms stay out of scope: name-only but asserted by nothing.
